title: Decimal integers past 64 bits are exact or refused, never rounded
notes: The Core schema reads a plain scalar that matches `[-+]?[0-9]+` as an integer and gives that pattern no upper bound (section 10.3.2). A library therefore either returns the exact integer or refuses the scalar with a limit error that says it is too large; turning it into a float, a string or a wrapped 64-bit number changes the data without a word. A library that reads it gives exactly the expected result; one that refuses it says so with a limit error. A crash, a hang, a wrong result, or more than the stated time or memory fails. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The values sit just past each 64-bit limit, then at thirty and a hundred digits, so a reader that wraps, rounds to a double or keeps a string shows which step it stops at.

provenance.reference: Integers past 64 bits read as floats (1.8446744073709552e+19), as strings or as rounded numbers in several libraries; a refusal with a limit error would be correct, and this case allows it.
